step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identified external data sources node (Data Sources) on the top left.
2. Identified two consumer/user nodes on the lower left (one representing people/agents and another representing web/system clients).
3. Identified the load balancing tier (ELB) receiving traffic from Data Sources.
4. Identified the central compute cluster labeled K8S (running microservices like Keycloak, Jupyter, Kong on EC2).
5. Identified messaging component (MQ / Amazon MQ) connected bidirectionally to K8S.
6. Identified database connectivity components: VPC Peering and MongoDB Atlas (ThirdParty) at the bottom connected to K8S.
7. Identified standalone database/cache services on the right: RDS (Postgres) and Redis (ElastiCache).
8. Traced all visual arrow paths and directionalities to build the edges and assigned sequences.

graph.name: Intellect Design Fabric Data Platform Architecture
graph.notes: Architecture showing data ingestion from multiple sources into a Kubernetes cluster via ELB, using Amazon MQ for decoupling, VPC Peering for MongoDB Atlas access, and RDS/ElastiCache for persistent storage and session caching.

nodes.name: Data Sources
nodes.notes: Crawled external data sources, regulatory, and social media data

nodes.name: ELB
nodes.notes: Elastic Load Balancer fanning out ingestion traffic

nodes.name: Consumers (Web)
nodes.notes: Insurance carrier systems and web applications

nodes.name: K8S
nodes.notes: Kubernetes cluster on EC2 running Keycloak, Jupyter Notebooks, Kong API Gateway, and microservices

nodes.name: MQ
nodes.notes: Amazon MQ for message buffering between processing pipelines

nodes.name: VPC Peering
nodes.notes: Private network connection between AWS VPC and MongoDB Atlas VPC

nodes.name: MongoDB Atlas
nodes.notes: MongoDB Atlas storing processed entity risk profile data

nodes.name: RDS
nodes.notes: Amazon RDS Postgres for Kong API Gateway and Keycloak authentication metadata

nodes.name: REDIS
nodes.notes: ElastiCache Redis for session and user cache management

edges.notes: Data Sources send ingestion traffic into ELB
ELB fans out traffic to microservices inside the Kubernetes cluster
Agents connect to Kong API Gateway inside K8S cluster
Web consumers connect to Kong API Gateway inside K8S cluster
K8S microservices push messages to Amazon MQ
K8S pipeline microservices consume messages from Amazon MQ
K8S queries/writes routed through VPC Peering
VPC Peering connects to MongoDB Atlas
Return traffic from VPC Peering to K8S
Direct persistent data push from K8S processing to MongoDB Atlas
